title: Expressing Wants & Prices
intro: Once toddlers master basic signals (Hello, Yes, No), their next big milestone is expressing desires and asking for things. Today we add 3 fundamental desire/transaction words and mix them with Lesson 1.

words.babyAnalogy: Reaching out hands towards something they want.
words.actionTag: Put any noun before it: 'Coffee beku' (I want coffee), 'Water beku'.

words.babyAnalogy: Pushing a toy or plate away gently.
words.actionTag: Say 'Auto beda' (Don't want auto) or 'Sugar beda' (No sugar).

words.babyAnalogy: Pointing inquisitively at something in a shop window.
words.actionTag: Point at any fruit, vegetable, or item and ask 'Eshtu?'.

combos.context: Ordering coffee at a Darshini or cafe.

combos.meaning: Don't want auto / No auto needed

combos.context: Combining Illa (Lesson 1) + Beda (Lesson 2) for strong polite refusal.
Combining Haudu (Lesson 1) + Beku (Lesson 2) for enthusiastic agreement.

quiz.scenario: You're buying tender coconut (elaneeru) at a roadside stall.
quiz.question: How do you ask 'How much?'

quiz.scenario: Someone tries to sell you an item you don't want.
quiz.question: How do you say 'No, don't want!' (2-word combo)?

quiz.scenario: Your colleague asks if you want filter coffee, and you really do!
quiz.question: How do you say 'Yes, want!'?
